_meta: A row of 8-bit pixel brightness values and a brightening offset, used to show why pixel arithmetic must saturate (clamp to the 0..255 range) rather than wrap around in the fixed-width integer, as naive uint8 math does. An 8-bit channel stores a value from 0 to 255. When you brighten an image you add an offset to every pixel, and some pixels are already near the top of the range, so the sum exceeds 255. In modular fixed-width integer arithmetic -- the default for a uint8 array in many languages and libraries -- the result wraps: 255 + 1 becomes 0, and 250 + 30 becomes 24. That is catastrophic for an image, because the very brightest pixels (the ones that overflow) wrap around to near-black, so a highlight turns into a dark speck and brightening the image punches black holes in exactly its lightest areas. The intended behavior is saturating arithmetic: a sum above 255 is clamped to 255 and a difference below 0 is clamped to 0, so brightening can only make a pixel brighter (up to pure white) and never flips it dark. pixels is the row of original 0..255 values; offset is the amount added to brighten. These are the fixture; the raw (unclamped) sums, the wrapped uint8 results, and the saturated (clamped) results are computed.
